newsitem.title: FINLAND: Partek sees Sisu synergy limited.
newsitem.headline: Partek sees Sisu synergy limited.

text.p: Partek CEO Christoffer Taxell said on Wednesday the synergy benefits from its planned merger with state vehicle manufacturer Sisu Oy would be less than 100 million markka.
"There is a limited number of direct synergies and they will not materialise during the first year," Taxell told a news conference.
Asked to specify the synergies and size of cost savings Partek expected from the deal, he said: "They are below 100 million markka", but gave no time frame.

Taxell said there were few overlapping operations in the companies, and when asked about any possible short term costs for Partek in the deal, said: "I don't see it increasing the costs dramatically, not even temporarily."
"There are no direct operational cost savings in personnel in sight," Taxell said.
He declined to give more details about Partek's plans for its pre-cast concrete business, which Partek said in the merger statement could now head towards independence.
Trade and Industry minister Antti Kalliomaki told the news conference the state had no plan to sell the 30 percent stake it will hold in the new group.
"It is not in our interest or intention to give up our holding in the new group," he said.
Taxell said the deal was struck on Partek's lead: "We have shown quite a lot of initiative in this."
